tests.title: mcpserve/go.mod declares the module, the root replace and exactly the two direct requirements
given: the root module's internal/policy test helpers (go mod edit -json, directSet, validateAllowlist, parseGoMod)
tests.when: the policy test reads mcpserve/go.mod and the root go.mod
then: module path is github.com/agent-fox-dev/agentkit-go/mcpserve and go is 1.27
exactly one replace maps github.com/agent-fox-dev/agentkit-go to "../"
the direct set is exactly the root module and github.com/modelcontextprotocol/go-sdk
the SDK version equals the root go.mod's version
validateAllowlist(direct, approvedDeps + mcpserve path) reports no violation
tests.pseudocode: m = goModEdit('mcpserve'); assert m.Module.Path == '.../mcpserve' && m.Go == '1.27'; assert replaces == {root: '../'}; assert directSet('mcpserve') == {root, sdk}; assert version(sdk, mcpserve) == version(sdk, root); assert validateAllowlist(direct, approvedDeps+modulePaths) == nil

tests.title: mcpserve's module graph adds no module the root graph lacks

tests.when: the two module-path sets are compared
then: mcpserve's set minus the root's set, with the mcpserve path removed, is empty
tests.pseudocode: diff = paths(mcpserve) - paths(root) - {mcpservePath}; assert diff == empty

tests.title: mcpserve holds one package named mcpserve with only allowed imports and no cmd directory
given: the mcpserve directory

then: exactly one package, named mcpserve, is listed
no main package and no mcpserve/cmd directory exist
every non-test import is the standard library, agentkit, core, mcp or wire of the root, or go-sdk mcp or jsonrpc
tests.pseudocode: pkgs = goList('./...'); assert len(pkgs)==1 && pkgs[0].Name=='mcpserve'; for imp in nonTestImports: assert imp in allowlist or isStdlib(imp)

tests.title: Every non-context error from New, ServeStdio and ServeLoopback is prefixed "mcpserve: "
given: a nil runner, a runner whose tool has a non-object schema, and a stdio session fed an over-limit frame
a loopback listen/random failure injected through the package's test seam
tests.when: New, ServeStdio and ServeLoopback are each driven to a non-context failure
then: each err.Error() starts with "mcpserve: "
tests.pseudocode: for err in [New(nil,{}), New(badSchemaRunner,{}), ServeStdio(oversizeInput), ServeLoopback(failingListen)]: assert hasPrefix(err.Error(), 'mcpserve: ')

tests.title: New with a nil runner returns nil and the exact refusal message
given: no runner
tests.when: mcpserve.New(nil, Options{}) is called
then: the server is nil
the error message is exactly "mcpserve: Runner is nil"
tests.pseudocode: s, err = New(nil, Options{}); assert s == nil; assert err.Error() == 'mcpserve: Runner is nil'

tests.title: tools/list returns exactly the runner's tools with verbatim names, descriptions and JSON-equal schemas
given: a real Runner over several tools with differing schemas (built-in tools and code_mode)
a Server connected to an SDK/mcp.Connect client over in-process pipes
tests.when: the client sends tools/list
then: the count and the set of names equal r.Tools()
each description is equal verbatim
each inputSchema is JSON-equal to json.Marshal(tool.InputSchema)
outputSchema, annotations and _meta are absent from every listed tool
tests.pseudocode: listed = client.ListTools(); for t in r.Tools(): l = byName[t.Name]; assert l.Description==t.Description; assert jsonEqual(l.InputSchema, marshal(t.InputSchema)); assert l.OutputSchema==nil && l.Annotations==nil && l.Meta==nil

tests.title: A tool with a nil InputSchema is listed with {"type":"object"}
given: a runner with one tool whose InputSchema is nil
tests.when: the client sends tools/list
then: that tool's inputSchema is JSON-equal to {"type":"object"}
tests.pseudocode: assert jsonEqual(list[0].InputSchema, '{"type":"object"}')

tests.title: New refuses a tool whose schema cannot be served and names the tool without panicking

tests.pseudocode: for r in cases: s, err = New(r, {}); assert s==nil; assert hasPrefix(err.Error(), 'mcpserve: tool "bad": input schema')

no tools/list_changed notification is received
tests.pseudocode: s = New(r); r.slice[0].Description='x'; r.slice = r.slice[:0]; assert listed == original; assert r.toolsCalls == 1

tests.title: initialize reports the configured or default server info and the instructions

tests.title: A runner with no tools yields a working server with an empty tool list

tests.title: tools/call reaches Runner.Call exactly once with byte-identical arguments, or empty when absent

tests.title: Result content is LLMText followed by every TextBlock in order, isError is !OK
given: a runner tool returning a generated core.ToolResult

then: Content length is 1 + number of TextBlocks
Content[0].Text equals res.LLMText() and the rest are the TextBlock texts in order
non-text blocks are dropped
IsError equals !res.OK
structuredContent is absent

tests.title: Runner failures arrive as isError results, never as protocol errors

tests.title: Cancelling a request or ending the session cancels the runner call, which returns aborted

tests.title: mcp.Pool over loopback HTTP runs code_mode whose nested read_file passes the Guard

tests.title: The harness fills its sandbox with exactly one sandbox.Open and no Create, Sync or Tools call
given: the examples/harness non-test sources and an offline run
tests.when: a structural test counts calls and the offline account is read
then: exactly one sandbox.Open call exists
no Provider.Create, Sandbox.Sync or Sandbox.Tools call exists
sources are chosen as GitRepo{Depth:1}, LocalDir{ExcludeGit:true} or LocalDir{Path: sample}
the account contains "filled the workspace from the sample project"
tests.pseudocode: assert count(calls,'sandbox.Open')==1; assert count(calls,'.Create'|'.Sync'|'.Tools')==0; assert contains(out,'filled the workspace from the sample project')

tests.title: The harness uses guard.Allow and faux helpers, with no guard.Restricted call or faux.Turn literal

then: guard.Allow(allowed...) is called

tests.title: examples/harness/go.mod requires mcpserve with a replace and lists the SDK only as indirect

then: it requires github.com/agent-fox-dev/agentkit-go/mcpserve v0.0.0

tests.pseudocode: m = goModEdit('examples/harness'); assert req(mcpserve).Version=='v0.0.0'; assert replace(mcpserve)=='../../mcpserve'; assert req(sdk).Indirect==true

tests.title: The harness example runs offline end to end through mcpserve

then: output contains "filled the workspace from the sample project"
output contains "imported 12 tools over MCP: agentkit__code_mode, agentkit__edit_file, agentkit__execute"
output contains "verdict: pass" and "Harness example completed successfully"

tests.pseudocode: out, code = run(['--harness','scripted', ...]); for s in expected: assert contains(out,s); assert code==0

tests.title: An embedder serves code_mode over loopback, a pool client runs a script, and Close refuses further connections
given: a workspace from workspace.Open with a known file
tools from tools.For wrapped by code_mode, a Runner with a recording Guard, a real Server
tests.when: ServeLoopback is called, mcp.Pool connects with URL and bearer token, lists tools and calls code_mode with a script calling read_file, then ep.Close() is called
then: the endpoint URL is http://127.0.0.1:<port>/mcp with a 48-character token
the call result is OK and holds the file content
the Guard recorded the code_mode call and the nested read_file call
after Close a TCP connect to the port is refused

tests.title: A harness spawns the program as a child and uses its tools over stdio until EOF
given: the test binary re-executed with a marker environment variable that builds a Runner and Server and calls ServeStdio
mcp.Pool with ServerConfig.Command (skipped on Windows)
tests.when: the pool connects, lists tools, calls one, then closes the connection
then: the tools are listed and the call returns the runner's text
the child's stdin is closed by the pool and every owed reply was written
the child exits with status 0

tests.title: An unauthenticated request is refused with 401 and a disallowed execute call comes back as a blocked isError result
given: a live endpoint over a Runner whose Guard allows only some programs
a capturing slog handler as Logger
tests.when: an initialize POST is sent without the token, then mcp.Pool connects with the token and calls execute with a disallowed program
then: the unauthenticated request gets 401 with WWW-Authenticate: Bearer and a Warn record with the peer and no header value is logged
the execute call returns a result with isError true whose text carries blocked_by_policy and the guard's reason, not a protocol error
one Info "tool call" record with ok=false is logged

tests.title: The harness example runs offline end to end through sandbox.Open, the Runner and mcpserve
given: the examples/harness program built with the scripted harness and the local provider
no network access
tests.when: the program is run offline against the sample project
then: it prints "filled the workspace from the sample project" and "MCP server at http://127.0.0.1:"
the scripted harness imports 12 tools over MCP and its faux code_mode turn runs through the runner over the sandbox proxies
it prints "verdict: pass" and "Harness example completed successfully"
the process exits 0 and the endpoint and sandbox are closed
